problem.label: The Problem
problem.title: Philadelphia's tax code wasn't built for the modern workforce
problem.intro1: Starting in 2026, all businesses in Philadelphia are about to be hit with a new—and probably surprise—tax bill.
problem.intro2: For the last 10 years, the smallest businesses in Philadelphia had a shield from the regressive Business Income and Receipts Tax, lovingly known as BIRT.
problem.intro3: That shield allowed them to start and grow into a business that could support themselves, their family, their community, and employ other Philadelphians.
problem.scale_text: While this information is public, most people don't realize the scale of the impact it's about to have on Philadelphians who run a small business as a way to simply survive.

impact_card.conclusion: That's between 1 and 3 months' rent for many Philadelphians—and they simply can't afford it.

thomas_quote.text1: I don't think we realize how catastrophic this is gonna be, [and] not just for small businesses.
thomas_quote.text2: Us getting rid of the $100,000 exemption while simultaneously not reducing the net income portion of BIRT will make it so that everybody [...] will leave Philadelphia.

problem.system_title: A system problem, not a rate problem
problem.system_text1: Philadelphia's two-class tax system treats every corporation and non-corporation the same: whether you're a solo freelancer, a 50-person partnership, or a large corporation like Comcast.
problem.system_text2: This means individual business owners face double taxation on income already captured by the Net Profits Tax, while corporations do not.
problem.callout: We are taxing working families out of their homes.

brooks_quote.text: We're going to see many businesses that have never filed taxes before trying to figure out how or where to file these taxes...I don't even know how many of them will know this is happening.
brooks_quote.attribution: — Council Member Kendra Brooks, a former small business owner

solution.label: The Solution
solution.title: The LIFT Act
solution.subtitle: Fix the system. Create a tax class for Laborers (Independent Contractors), Individual Enterprises & Family Enterprises (Individually owned LLCs).

exempt.title: Exempt from BIRT
exempt.description: Removes BIRT for the LIFT class completely.

legal.title: Legally Sound
legal.description: Meets Pennsylvania Constitution's Uniformity Clause requirements. Confirmed by Philadelphia Law Dept.

local.title: Keeps Money Local
local.description: Every dollar retained by a Philadelphian becomes three dollars in local spending.
